cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine build the work-in-progress schedule for HANGS Construction: how far along each job is.
First, it reads five contracts and the books. Last month's schedule ties.
A change order changes a contract's price. One the owner hasn't signed is left out.
Next, it checks every cost against its job's budget. An $18,750 framing bill was charged to the wrong job.
Next, how complete each job is. One estimate is out of date, and one job now shows a loss.
Earned revenue follows how complete each job is. Billing ahead of that is overbilling; behind it, underbilling. The whole expected loss is recorded now.
Last, it writes the workpapers and an unsigned memo for the controller, the head of accounting.

All done. Earned revenue is about $2.42 million against $2.38 million billed. Three journal entries, corrections to the books, are proposed, including a billing adjustment of about $96,100. Four items need a person. Nothing is posted until the controller approves.
